name: OmniNexus
tag: Looks at a problem across mechanical, electrical, software and other fields and proposes one combined fix.

scenarios.title: Pumps keep overheating
scenarios.ask: {pumps} pumps at our water station overheat on days above {temp}. Find a fix that works across disciplines.
steps: Mechanical
Bearing temperatures are normal. The motors run hot, not the pumps.
Electrical
Supply voltage sags 6% at peak load, so motors draw more current.
Controls
All {pumps} pumps start together at shift change, causing the sag.
Building
The pump room vents are undersized for days above {temp}.
Synthesis
Combined fix: stagger starts by 90 seconds and add one exhaust fan.
followups: Why not just buy bigger motors?
Bigger motors would still start at the same time and still sit in a hot room. The combined fix costs less and solves the cause.
Each discipline's part is written for that engineer to review and sign off.

scenarios.title: Add solar to an older roof
scenarios.ask: Can we add {kw} of solar to our {age}-year-old warehouse roof?
steps: Structural
Panels and racking add about {=round(kw * 60)} kg spread across the roof.
Roofing
At {age} years, the membrane may need replacing within the panels' life.
Electrical
Checked the main panel for back-feed limits. Larger systems often need a service upgrade.
Finance
Compared re-roofing first with installing now and moving panels later.
Synthesis
Built one plan that orders roof, electrical and solar work.

result.title: Roof and solar plan
rows: Recommended when roof age is over 15 years; yours is {age}

followups: Does it replace a structural engineer?
No. It prepares the questions and numbers so the engineer's review is faster.
What if we lease the building?
The plan adds a short section on what to agree with the landlord about the roof and wiring.

scenarios.title: Quiet a noisy product
scenarios.ask: Customers say our {product} is too loud. It measures {db}. Target is {target}.
steps: Acoustics
Most noise comes from blade tones and panel rattle.
Mechanical
Adding rubber mounts cuts panel rattle by about 3 dB.
Software
A smoother fan speed curve removes a hum at the mid setting.
Industrial design
A curved air path lowers blade tone by about 2 dB.
Synthesis
Ranked the fixes by cost and how much noise each removes.
followups: Yes. A 3 dB drop halves the sound energy, and most people notice it.
What if the fixes don't close the gap?
The plan lists the next options, like a slower, larger fan, with cost and size trade-offs.
